title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 207 (Conduct of inspection and inquiry)

content.overview: Section 207 provides that where a Registrar or inspector calls for the books of account and other books and papers under section 206, it shall be the duty of every director, officer or other employee of the company to produce them and to furnish such statements, information or explanations as the Registrar or inspector may require, and to render all assistance in connection with the inspection. The Registrar or inspector may, with such assistance as may be required, make or cause to be made copies of books and papers, and may enter any place where books are kept if there are reasonable grounds. Failure to produce books, to furnish information, or destruction or falsification of records attracts the penal consequences stated in the section.
content.glance: On s. 206 inspection/inquiry: directors, officers and employees must produce books, furnish explanations and assist; Registrar/inspector may copy records and enter premises on reasonable grounds; non-production, non-answer and destruction/falsification attract penalties.
content.study: Where a Registrar or inspector calls for the books of account and other books and papers under section 206, it shall be the duty of every director, officer or other employee of the company to produce all such books and papers relating to the company and to furnish such statements, information or explanations relating to the affairs of the company as the Registrar or inspector may require, and otherwise to give to the Registrar or inspector all assistance in connection with the inspection. The Registrar or inspector making an inspection or inquiry under section 206 may, during the course of such inspection or inquiry—(a) make or cause to be made copies of books of account and other books and papers; or (b) place or cause to be placed any marks of identification in such books in token of the inspection having been made. If the Registrar or inspector has reasonable ground to believe that books are being kept at any place, he may enter that place. Current-law framing: confirm a s. 206 call; apply the duty to produce, explain and assist; note copying and entry powers; apply consequences for non-compliance, destruction or falsification. Inspection under ss. 206–207 remains distinct from formal investigation under ss. 210 and 212.

sections.heading: Duty to Produce and Assist
sections.body: Every director, officer or other employee must produce books and papers, furnish statements/information/explanations, and render all assistance in connection with the inspection under s. 206.

sections.heading: Copying and Identification Marks
sections.body: Registrar or inspector may make copies of books and papers and place marks of identification in token of inspection.

sections.heading: Entry of Premises
sections.body: If there are reasonable grounds to believe books are kept at a place, the Registrar or inspector may enter that place.

sections.heading: Consequences of Non-Compliance
sections.body: Failure to produce or answer, and destruction or falsification of records, attract the penalties the section provides.

examples.title: Refusal to produce
examples.body: During a s. 206 inspection, a director refuses to produce the statutory registers. Section 207 imposes a duty on every director, officer and employee to produce books and papers and furnish explanations; non-compliance attracts the section’s consequences.

examples.title: Entry on reasonable grounds
examples.body: The Registrar has reasonable ground to believe that accounting books are kept at a branch office not disclosed in the registered-office records. Section 207 permits entry of that place for the purposes of the inspection.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 207 authorise a full SFIO-style investigation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 207 governs the conduct of inspection and inquiry under section 206. Formal investigation is under sections 210 and 212. The duties and powers in s. 207 are those of inspection and inquiry, not of a completed investigation order.

distinctions.title: Conduct of inspection (s. 207) vs power to call for information (s. 206)
distinctions.left: How inspection/inquiry is conducted; duties of officers; entry and copying
distinctions.right: Registrar’s power to initiate the call for information, inspection and inquiry

misconceptions.trap: Only the company secretary must cooperate with a Registrar’s inspection.
misconceptions.correction: Section 207 imposes the duty on every director, officer or other employee of the company to produce books, furnish explanations and assist.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 207 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm s. 206 call. II. Apply duty to produce, explain and assist. III. Note copying and entry powers. IV. Apply non-compliance consequences. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Inspection facts; duty breached or complied with; entry/copying issues; precise relief.

examTips: Duty on every director, officer and employee.
Copying and entry on reasonable grounds.

learningObjectives: State the duties of officers during inspection under s. 207.
Explain copying, entry and non-compliance consequences.
enhancement.definition: Section 207 requires every director, officer and employee to produce books, furnish explanations and assist during a s. 206 inspection or inquiry, and empowers the Registrar or inspector to copy records and enter premises on reasonable grounds.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Inspection powers are effective only if officers are under a clear duty to produce, explain and assist, backed by penal consequences for obstruction or falsification.
essentialIngredients: Duty to produce books and furnish explanations
Power to copy books and place identification marks
Power to enter premises on reasonable grounds
Penalties for non-production, non-answer, destruction or falsification
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 207 is the conduct and duty companion to the s. 206 initiating power.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm s. 206 context; apply duties; note entry and penalties.

verification.note: Section-text level; case-law verification separate; no new citations invented.

distinctions: Conduct of inspection (s. 207) vs power to call for information (s. 206)
